the influence of impurities on the cohesion of synthetic NaCl crystals.
the influence of foreign additives on cohesion and ultramicroscopic crystallization of synthetic sodium chloride.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of the foreign substances is a function of the size, shape and concentration of the foreign substance.
the mechanical strength and the microstructure of the synthetic salt crystals are not only influenced by their purity but are also influenced by the presence of impurities.
, for the most part, the effects of impurities are to increase the cohesion strength, and the effects are most pronounced in the case of impurities which are molecularly dispersed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the influence of the additives is not a simple function of the lattice parameter of the impurity, as was previously assumed, but depends on the state of dispersion of the impurity in the crystal.
the influence of impurities on cohesion and on the microcrystallization of synthetic rock salt is a function of the solubility product of the impurity and the size of the impurity molecules.
the mechanical properties of single crystals are influenced by foreign ions in the crystal lattice in a way which is dependent on their concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of the impurity ions does not change the nature of the crystal growth mechanism, but it does change the kinetics of growth and the resulting morphology of the crystals.
